desc: Parse input, attach original indices, sort intervals by right endpoint, and build arrays of (l, r, w, origIdx).
Implement binary search (bisect) to find for each interval i the largest j with r_j < l_i (strict, since shared endpoints overlap).

Implement DP: dp[i][k] = best (weight, path) using intervals up to i with at most k chosen; transitions are skip interval i or take it (combine with dp[p[i]][k-1]); keep full table since take-transition needs state at p[i].
Define comparison logic: prefer higher weight; on tie prefer lexicographically smaller sorted tuple of original indices (Python tuple comparison handles prefix rule).
Return list(dp[n][4].path) — "at most 4" semantics via skip transition; weights positive so empty path never optimal.

Test with provided examples plus edge cases: single interval, all overlapping, weight ties with different index sets, boundary-touching intervals, randomized brute-force cross-check, and n = 5*10^4 performance check.
